articles.title: Large scale, open data, and a big tent: Advancing macrosystems ecology through collaboration, transparency, and inclusion
articles.desc: This Special Feature examines how macrosystems ecology advances understanding of ecological patterns and processes that operate across nested spatial, temporal, and organizational scales, from microsite to continent. This Special Feature synthesizes 10 contributions spanning freshwater and terrestrial systems, plants and animals, and methods development through empirical synthesis, showing that continental observational networks (e.g., NEON, USA‐NPN) and coordinated citizen science enable questions no single team or dataset could address alone. These studies reveal that ecological patterns are strongly scale‐ and assemblage‐dependent, that trait‐based and intraspecific approaches increasingly complement species‐level descriptions, and that open software tools and shared leadership models are as essential as the data themselves. Collectively, the papers highlight three lessons: cross‐scale linkages are the unit of analysis in macrosystems ecology; trait distributions provide a natural currency for cross‐scale and cross‐continent comparison; and the data revolution is inseparable from a parallel revolution in how teams collaborate, communicate, and engage the public. The collection calls for cross‐network synthesis across continents, operationalization of CARE principles alongside FAIR norms, translation of continental‐scale findings into actionable science, and structural investment in the next generation of macrosystems ecologists. articles.desc: The rice-wheat cropping system is central to India's food security. Net ecosystem exchange, ecosystem respiration, and gross primary productivity were measured at two rice-wheat cropping sites using eddy covariance. The system acted as a net carbon sink at both sites.

articles.title: Marsh Width and Elevation Govern Lateral Dynamics in Coastal Wetlands
articles.desc: Coastal wetland persistence is controlled by coupled interactions among vegetation, geomorphology, and hydrodynamics under sea level rise. We quantified salt marsh lateral erosion and migration over 80+ years across 75 km of Long Island's south shore.

articles.title: Organic Matter Redox Status Predicts Methane Production in Boreal Peatland Ecosystems
articles.desc: Boreal peatlands are important locations of carbon storage, but the mechanisms controlling methane production in these ecosystems are not fully understood. Reduction of redox-active organic matter predicted methane production across boreal peatland ecosystems.

articles.title: Biodiversity, Fisheries, and Climate Benefits of Mangroves: A Nature-Based Solution for Ocean Ecosystems
articles.desc: Mangrove ecosystems are globally recognized as biodiversity hotspots and critical components of coastal resilience, providing nursery habitats, carbon sequestration, and shoreline stabilization. This review synthesizes biodiversity and fisheries functions of mangroves as a nature-based solution.

articles.title: Linking Scrub Mangroves Long-Term (2012-2021) Foliar Net Primary Productivity and their Spatial Distribution in the Everglades (Florida, USA): A Conceptual Model
articles.desc: Mangrove ecotypes reflect the critical role of environmental factors in regulating functional and structural properties. We evaluate decadal foliar net primary productivity of scrub mangroves in the lower Everglades.

articles.title: Isolating Effects of Temperature and Light on Nutrient Acquisition by Biofilm and Bryophyte Communities in Arctic Spring-Stream Ecosystems
articles.desc: Light and temperature are strong drivers of ecosystem processes seasonally coupled in most ecosystems. Arctic spring-streams provide an exception due to relatively constant water temperatures and extreme annual light fluctuations.

articles.title: Isoscapes of Particulate Organic Matter d13C and d15N Values in Chilean Coastal Waters
articles.desc: Stable isotope analysis is widely used in modern marine ecology but depends on accounting for spatial and temporal variability in baseline values. We present the first observation-based isoscapes for particulate organic matter in the southeastern Pacific.

articles.title: Tidal Flats as Organic Matter Accumulation Zones: Depositional Patterns and Effects of Different Types of Detritus
articles.desc: Tidal flats are recognized as ecosystems with potential to contribute to climate change mitigation through carbon accumulation. This study characterizes spatio-temporal patterns of wrack deposition and effects of marine and terrestrial detritus on sediment organic matter.

articles.title: Season-Specific Effects of Marine Heatwaves on Macrofaunal Community Composition and Ecosystem Processes
articles.desc: Marine heatwaves increasingly modify marine ecosystems. We conducted four repetitive laboratory experiments across seasons to investigate effects of seasonal marine heatwaves on natural benthic communities, finding season-specific changes in community metabolism.

articles.title: The Too-Few Elephant Problem: Quantitative Analysis of Historical Elephant Tree-Toppling Rates Across Africa
articles.desc: Elephants were a major driver of tree stem mortality in Africa but their impacts are now spatially constrained. We collated empirical data on treefall in ecosystems with and without elephants and predicted past tree loss spatially, finding elephants knock down 5.4% of trees per annum on average.

articles.title: In Situ Evidence for Quantitative Nitrogen Fixation in a Temperate Perennial Grass Ecosystem
articles.desc: Biological nitrogen fixation is an important terrestrial ecosystem N input. We measured non-symbiotic nitrogen fixation in field mesocosms with mature switchgrass, estimating inputs of 2-12 kg N per hectare per year.

articles.title: Long-Term Reindeer Exclusion Leads to Higher Carbon Storage and Less Recalcitrant Carbon Compounds in Boreal Forest Soils
articles.desc: Dry unproductive Scots pine forests provide conditions where ground-dwelling lichens thrive, a crucial winter forage for reindeer. We assessed impacts of 50+ years of reindeer exclusion on soil organic carbon quantity and quality in northern Finland.

articles.title: Nitrogen and Phosphorus Availability Mediates the Effects of Bottom-Up Limitation on Orb-Weaver Spider Traits in an Amazonian Rainforest
articles.desc: Nutrient availability is a key driver of terrestrial ecosystem functioning and food web structure. We tested whether alleviating nutrient limitation affects predator traits using a large-scale factorial fertilisation experiment in the Amazon.

articles.title: Diverse Impacts of Urbanization on Vegetation Growth and Its Driving Factors in Ten Global Megacities
articles.desc: Understanding how urbanization affects vegetation growth within global megacities remains underexplored. We compared urban expansion, vegetation index trends, and driving factors across ten global megacities from 2000 to 2018.

articles.title: Ditch Sediment Contribution to Remove Geogenic Nitrogen in a Reclaimed Area (Po River Delta, Italy)
articles.desc: Networks of drainage ditches play a crucial role in processing nitrogen loads. This study investigated the nitrogen removal capacity of ditch sediments in a reclaimed area with paleo-marsh peat lenses releasing geogenic nitrogen.

articles.title: Management Reshapes Belowground Productivity Allocation Across Global Resource Gradients
articles.desc: Belowground carbon allocation regulates soil carbon inputs and ecosystem resilience. Using a global terrestrial net primary production archive across 456 sites, unmanaged grasslands allocated substantially more production belowground than managed grasslands.

articles.title: Responses of Microbial Communities and Enzymatic Activities to Warming and Nitrogen Addition During Fine-Root Litter Decomposition on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
articles.desc: Fine-root decomposition plays a critical role in regulating the carbon cycle. An 18-month field manipulation experiment investigated how warming and nitrogen addition affected fine-root decomposition through litter-associated microbial communities.

articles.title: Divergent Trajectories: Freshwater Rehydration is Associated with Both Increasing and Decreasing Marsh Productivities in the Florida Everglades
articles.desc: Hydrology is a key variable of ecosystem development in wetlands. We quantified long-term changes in vegetation and phosphorus retention during freshwater rehydration in Everglades National Park, revealing divergent productivity trajectories among sites.

articles.title: Role of Fish Communities in Incorporating Methane-Derived Carbon in a Tropical Floodplain Lake System
articles.desc: Floodplain systems play a key role in methane emissions, part of which can be incorporated into methanotrophic bacteria biomass and transferred to higher trophic levels. We used stable isotopes to investigate fish community incorporation of methane-derived carbon.

articles.title: Testing the Influence of Internal Stem Decay and Topography on Biomass and Carbon Stock Estimates in Mongolia's Boreal Forest
articles.desc: Improvement of forest biomass estimates is of outstanding interest for the global carbon cycle. We tested the influence of biomass loss due to internal stem decay and topography on aboveground biomass in southern boreal forests of Mongolia.

articles.title: Endophytic Phomopsis liquidambaris recruits nitrogen-fixing taxa by altering the rhizosphere metabolites of Oryza sativa L.
articles.desc: The endophytic fungus Phomopsis liquidambaris could optimize the community structure of nitrogen-transforming microorganisms in rhizosphere soil of rice under low-nitrogen conditions via rhizosphere metabolites.

articles.title: Rhizosphere microbiome analysis revealed the role of Actinomycetes in vermicompost- and Piriformospora indica-mediated apple growth
articles.desc: Vermicompost application and Piriformospora indica colonization can both promote plant growth and reshape soil microbial populations. Actinomycetes, especially Streptomyces, identified as key contributor in promoting apple seedling growth.

articles.title: The interactive effect of silicon and calcium in inhibiting Na+ uptake and mitigating salt stress in wheat
articles.desc: Silicon alleviates salt stress in wheat but its interaction with calcium remains unclear. A Box-Behnken design investigated silicon, sodium, and calcium interactions on growth, ion homeostasis, and antioxidant capacity in wheat.

articles.title: Effects of short-term active restoration on soil organic carbon fractions and CAZyme family genes: a comparison between degraded and restored alpine grasslands
articles.desc: Active restoration is the primary approach for restoring degraded Qinghai-Tibet Plateau grasslands. Artificial restoration significantly increased soil organic carbon fractions and altered CAZyme gene abundance.

articles.title: Foliar Epichloe endophyte infection reshapes soil microbial communities across aggregate size fractions in ryegrass soils
articles.desc: Epichloe endophyte infection in grasses is known to reshape soil microbial diversity and composition. Bacterial and fungal communities across aggregate size fractions were characterized in ryegrass soils.

articles.title: From photosynthesis to grain formation: a comprehensive evaluation of phosphorus - lanthanum combined effects on mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) cultivation
articles.desc: Phosphorus deficiency is a major abiotic stress limiting crop production in mung bean. This study investigates interactive effects of phosphorus levels and foliar lanthanum on photosynthesis and seed quality.

articles.title: Biocrust mediates microbial residue carbon accumulation by augmenting soil organic carbon fractions under reduced tillage in the Northeast black soil region of China
articles.desc: Biological soil crusts promote soil carbon sequestration, yet their regulation of soil microbial residue carbon remains poorly understood. Reduced tillage promoted biocrusts and boosted microbial residue carbon.

articles.title: Effects of quicklime application rate on carbon mineralization in strongly acidic soil of Chinese fir plantations
articles.desc: Strongly acidic Chinese fir plantation soils face constraints in nutrient and carbon dynamics. Quicklime amendment exerted significant nonlinear, dose-dependent effects on soil carbon cycling.

articles.title: Rock moisture access contributes to hydrologic niche segregation among co-dominant woody plants
articles.desc: Bedrock can store substantial plant-available water, yet its role in hydrologic niche segregation and drought resilience remains unclear. We investigated this in the semiarid karst Edwards Plateau, Texas, among three co-dominant woody species.

articles.title: Intrinsic coordination trade-offs between functional traits and rhizosphere metabolites underpin plant adaptation to chronic grazing in an arid grassland
articles.desc: Long-term grazing in arid grasslands imposes multifactorial stressors that reshape plant functional traits and rhizosphere metabolite profiles. A 22-year grazing history revealed intrinsic coordination trade-offs.

articles.title: Dark septate endophyte colonization exceeds arbuscular mycorrhizal colonization across winter wheat production systems
articles.desc: Dark septate endophytes are widespread root-associated fungi, yet colonization patterns relative to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi remain poorly characterized. DSE colonization exceeded AMF across winter wheat systems.

articles.title: Leaf lipid traits reflect contrasting carbon allocation strategies between evergreen and deciduous trees
articles.desc: Leaf lipid concentration and richness across 53 subtropical tree species were examined in relation to leaf functional traits, differing between evergreen and deciduous species.

articles.title: Effects of ozone and combined organic-inorganic fertilization on soil nitrification in wheat rhizosphere: insights from an O3-FACE experiment
articles.desc: Ground-level ozone can indirectly affect soil processes by altering plant physiology. A two-year Free-Air ozone enrichment experiment investigated effects on soil nitrification in wheat rhizosphere.

articles.title: Plant diversity promotes soil carbon sequestration via productivity pathways along elevational gradients
articles.desc: Grassland soil organic carbon is a major component of terrestrial carbon stocks. Plant diversity emerged as the dominant biotic factor associated with soil carbon accumulation along an elevational gradient in the Tianshan Mountains.

articles.title: Tree diversity and mycorrhizal type induce stronger shifts in fungal necromass than in soil carbon and nitrogen across the soil profile over a decade of afforestation
articles.desc: Tree species richness can enhance soil carbon and nitrogen storage, mediated by mycorrhizal associations. Biodiversity effects were detected for microbial necromass over a decade-old tree diversity experiment.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of radial oxygen loss during rice seedling establishment in a stagnant deoxygenated agar medium
articles.desc: Successful seedling establishment under waterlogged conditions is crucial for growth and yield. We investigated how light affects radial oxygen loss dynamics during rice seedling establishment.

articles.title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi regulate plant-bacteria interactions for coupled PAH attenuation and Hg phytostabilization in co-contaminated soil
articles.desc: Co-contamination of organic pollutants and heavy metals is a severe issue in soil. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can form a critical linkage between plants and soil microbiome for coupled remediation.

articles.title: Catch-cropping leguminous green manure during fallow improves yield and quality of chili, tomato, and cucumber
articles.desc: Continuous cropping causes soil degradation and vegetable quality deterioration. Leguminous green manure incorporation improved soil properties, plant growth, yield, and quality across chili, tomato, and cucumber.

articles.title: Coupled effects of soil quality and pathogens on nature-based restoration of target plants in desertified alpine grasslands
articles.desc: Overgrazing has led to degradation in alpine grasslands. Soil properties, pathogens, seed banks, and plant community composition were investigated in lightly degraded and desertified alpine meadows and steppes.

articles.title: Grassland diversity of submontane valleys under influence of soil and management types
articles.desc: Grassland communities in submontane areas of temperate zones result from centuries of human activity. Soil moisture, fertility, and traditional management practices determined grassland diversity in Western Carpathians, Poland.

articles.title: Disentangling biotic and abiotic drivers of a neotropical mistletoe
articles.desc: Parasitic plants known as mistletoes form intricate networks of biotic interactions. We assessed climatic niche similarity between Psittacanthus robustus, its host trees, and seed dispersers, finding host trees primarily shape the parasite's spatial distribution.

articles.title: The effect of heat waves on pill bug Armadillidium vulgare risk-taking strategies
articles.desc: Global climate change is expected to increase temperature fluctuations, likely affecting animal behaviour in small-bodied ectotherms. We investigated how heat waves influence risk-taking behaviour in the common pill bug, finding reduced risk-taking under thermal stress.

articles.title: Species-specific patterns in fine-root traits and their coordination in the multidimensional root economics space at the Mongolian forest-steppe ecotone
articles.desc: Belowground strategies were elucidated using root functional traits and symbiotic associations for three dominant tree species in the bioclimatically sensitive forest-steppe ecotone of northern Mongolia.

articles.title: No evidence for thermal melanism in Canadian butterflies despite long-term lightening of wing colour
articles.desc: Climate change can alter ectotherm morphology. Using 991 museum specimens of 10 butterfly species collected across Canada over 54 years, we found no support for the thermal melanism hypothesis despite butterflies becoming paler over time.

articles.title: Increasing bird diversity in a landscape in transition
articles.desc: Rural depopulation across Mediterranean uplands has driven farmland extensification and landscape transitions, yet their medium-term impacts on birds remain poorly understood. We resurveyed 213 selected 2 km × 2 km grid cells in the Côa River basin (western Iberia) in 2023–2024, following protocols comparable to those applied in 1999–2005, ensuring consistent sampling across periods. Median alpha diversity increased by five species, a 28% gain, with total abundance rising as common taxa became more widespread. Gains were predominantly driven by forest-associated and generalist species, while farmland specialists showed stagnation or slight declines. We discuss how landscape transitions contributed to these biodiversity patterns including lower human density, reduced grazing pressure, and altered disturbance regimes. However, significant avian diversity gains occurred within apparently stable forest-cover mosaics, potentially masking broader ecological shifts.

articles.title: Beta diversity patterns of saproxylic beetle communities in Patagonian temperate forests reflect the influence of wood decay and environmental variability on the foraging preferences of woodpeckers
articles.desc: Woodpeckers prefer trees with higher beetle diversity, but composition of beetle assemblages in trees used for foraging was largely unknown. We assessed beta diversity patterns of saproxylic beetles in Patagonian temperate forests used by Magellanic woodpeckers.

articles.title: Land use and propolis composition: an analysis of the wax content of Apis mellifera propolis
articles.desc: Propolis is a plant-derived resin collected by honeybees. Using citizen-science samples from UK hives, we found land cover surrounding hives strongly correlates with wax content of propolis.

articles.title: Developing quantitative relationships between functional traits and performance of tropical seaweed
articles.desc: Trait-based ecology has deepened understanding of community response to environmental challenges. A field experiment on three tropical seaweed species linked functional traits directly to growth performance.

articles.title: Hyperabundance of a subordinate herbivorous gastropod causes localised overgrazing within kelp beds
articles.desc: Herbivory by grazing macro-invertebrates can cause extensive overgrazing of kelp beds when grazers reach hyperabundance. We observed barren patches caused by a subordinate periwinkle grazer, Lunella undulata, in eastern Tasmania.

articles.title: Evolutionary novelty shapes predator-mediated insect herbivory in exotic oaks
articles.desc: Phylogenetic distance between exotic and native plant species is a predictor of insect herbivory. We manipulated predator access on 18 exotic oak species, finding ant-mediated predation underlies the phylogenetic herbivory pattern.

articles.title: Host tissue stoichiometry links nutrient availability to parasite abundance in a piscivorous fish
articles.desc: Understanding how ecosystem nutrient availability influences parasites is challenging for trophically transmitted parasites in hosts at higher trophic levels. Digestive tissue nutrient stoichiometry linked basal nutrient availability to trematode parasite abundance in largemouth bass.

articles.title: Less cooperative belowground plant mutualists negatively affect aboveground herbivore growth and survival
articles.desc: Resource mutualists like nitrogen-fixing rhizobia can affect quality of plants for herbivores. High-quality rhizobium strains significantly improved survival of a generalist insect herbivore, the beet armyworm, feeding on clover.

articles.title: The impact of non-native trees on galling and herbivory in New York City across space and time
articles.desc: Native trees often host more arthropods than non-native trees. Across spatial and temporal scales in New York City, native trees supported far more galling species than long-established non-native trees.

articles.title: Bottom-up control of coral reef sponges: for better and for worse
articles.desc: Controversy over bottom-up versus top-down control of coral reef sponges has distracted from nuanced questions about their food supply. Sponge growth was faster in more nutrient-rich water but dense cyanobacteria blooms devastated sponge populations.

articles.title: Seasonal structure, multi-scale variance, and inter-annual consistency of plant phenology in a Neotropical perhumid forest
articles.desc: Plant phenology is a key determinant of tropical forest productivity and trophic dynamics. Ten years of phenological recordings from Los Tuxtlas, Mexico revealed seasonal forcing drives dominant phenological variation even in a near year-round rainfall climate.

articles.title: Environmental, reproductive, and nutrient drivers of three-dimensional growth in the forest lichen Lobaria pulmonaria
articles.desc: Measuring growth dynamics is fundamental to understanding lichen biology and ecology. An integrative reanalysis of published growth data identified bark pH, light, hydration, and reproductive investment as key drivers of Lobaria pulmonaria growth.

articles.title: Delayed hatching as a life-history response to intraguild predation: interspecific variation in predatory mites
articles.desc: Predator-induced hatching plasticity allows embryos to adjust hatching timing in response to predator cues. We compared delayed hatching responses among four phytoseiid mite species differing in cannibalism and diet specialisation.

articles.title: Legacy and live effects of ecosystem engineer differ across energy gradient, reversing net engineering outcome
articles.desc: Ecosystem engineers influence abiotic and biotic community properties. Live and legacy effects of the oyster Crassostrea virginica act in opposing directions across a physical energy gradient, reversing the net engineering effect on cordgrass.

articles.title: Plants adjust leaf senescence in response to light heterogeneity across branches
articles.desc: Leaf senescence may allow plants to use resorbed nitrogen for new growth. Sunflower experiments with shaded and unshaded branches showed senescence patterns consistent with a strategy that prioritizes competing with neighbors for light.

articles.title: Substrate type and termite discovery shape decomposition at the dry end of an African savanna rainfall gradient
articles.desc: Global decomposition studies show decomposition is primarily temperature-driven with rainfall playing a secondary role. Decomposition of wood, dung and grass along a semi-arid savanna rainfall gradient revealed substrate-dependent patterns and the role of termite discovery.

articles.title: The ethical costs of remotely sensing tropical forest understories
articles.desc: Spaceborne and airborne scanning technologies are revolutionizing the study of tropical forest understories. As these datasets rapidly expand, we argue for systematic ethical consideration of whether and how to reveal the information they contain.

articles.title: Declining cicadas
articles.desc: Commentary on declining cicada populations.

articles.title: Symbiosis without codiversification
articles.desc: Commentary on symbiosis and codiversification patterns.

articles.title: Ecosystem stability is shaped by resource-trait coordination under multiple interacting global change factors
articles.desc: Ecological communities are increasingly exposed to multiple anthropogenic drivers. Using a 13-year field experiment, the authors show that effects of up to four interacting global change factors on grassland productivity and stability are dynamically reorganized through time, partly through changes in species asynchrony and trait composition.

articles.title: Robert Ricklefs (1943-2026)
articles.desc: Polymath ecologist whose research and textbooks integrating ecology and evolution have inspired generations of students.

articles.title: Adaptive zones of feliforms and evolutionary regimes within terrestrial mammalian carnivores
articles.desc: The relationship between form and function of terrestrial carnivore dentition is inconsistent, despite repeated evolution of similar ecomorphologies. The authors compile a total-evidence phylogeny to identify three adaptive zones within feliforms.

articles.title: Ancient vocabulary for evolving cells
articles.desc: A comparative multi-omic study finds that family-biased repertoires of short regulatory DNA motifs remain conserved over greater evolutionary distances than motif sets associated with individual cell types.

articles.title: Flexible use of conserved motifs constrains genome access in cell type evolution
articles.desc: Applying deep-learning models to single-nucleus multi-omic sequencing data from flatworms and vertebrates, the authors propose sets of sequence motifs defining cell type families are evolutionarily stable.

articles.title: Vegetation overcompensation after late-spring frost is widespread across terrestrial ecosystems
articles.desc: Terrestrial vegetation can recover from late-spring frost and even compensate for frost-induced productivity losses. Reduced damage and enhanced regrowth jointly drive this overcompensation, predicted to become more prevalent with climate warming.

articles.title: Advancing the adoption of RNA interference-based biopesticides
articles.desc: This Review examines how reliability, regulation, public acceptance and advances in design and delivery will shape adoption of RNA interference-based biopesticides within integrated pest and disease management.

articles.title: Overcompensation of vegetation productivity after late-spring frost in the Northern Hemisphere
articles.desc: Following late-spring frost, vegetation often overcompensates through reduced damage and enhanced regrowth. This response is strengthening under climate warming and increasingly buffers the global terrestrial carbon sink.

articles.title: Publisher Correction: PAX-regulated self-organizing polarity drives procambial strand formation
articles.desc: In the version of this article initially published, there were graphical display errors in Figs. 1a, 2b, c, e, 3a–d, f, g, 4a–d, f, 5f, Extended Data Figs. 2, 7 which are now amended in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

articles.title: Ancient trees, different genetic legacies
articles.desc: Old and ancient trees should be preserved for their crucial roles in local ecosystems. Data from Glyptostrobus pensilis (Chinese swamp cypress) suggest ancient individuals are not particularly distinct genetically from younger individuals.

articles.title: CRISPR beyond biology: building a sustainable innovation system
articles.desc: Commentary on CRISPR innovation systems.

articles.title: A soybean transcriptome atlas reveals organ- and cell-type-specific sets of co-expressed transcription factors
articles.desc: Analysis of an integrated single-nucleus transcriptome from ten soybean organs reveals organ- and cell-type-specific co-expression of transcription factor genes.

articles.title: Decoding the landscape of cell-type-specific co-expressed transcription factors in soybean
articles.desc: The soybean single-cell transcriptome atlas, Tabula Glycine max, spans ten organs, revealing that co-expressed transcription factor genes define most cell types based on function and organ of origin.
